Subject: Initial demand profile + burst ask for Dedicated pool

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers looked promising. As we talked about, Zentauri is planning a phased rollout of our inference features across three product lines. Attached is a short forecast (sheet: "May-Oct") showing expected token throughput per feature and the burst windows for marketing launches.

Two quick asks so we can finalize internal sign-offs:
- Can Redwood guarantee a soft headroom allocation for repeatable weekly marketing spikes (we're estimating 4x baseline for 3 hours)?
- What does the autoscale pact look like for Dedicated customers where we need predictable throttling vs. graceful degradation?

We'd like to include this in the SOW so Procurement can move the contract forward. If it's easier, Ben/Engineering can join a short call to validate ops constraints.

Thanks,

Zentauri

Hi Maya — great to get the forecast, thanks.

High level answer to your two asks:
- Soft headroom: yes — we can allocate a "shoulder" pool (configurable sizing) that you can draw from for predictable marketing spikes. We typically model this as a reserved slab + ephemeral credit balance to cover N hours of 4x activity per week.
- Autoscale pact: we propose a two-tier approach: guaranteed baseline (reserved GPUs) + elastic headroom (ephemeral/shoulder) with explicit eviction and preemption SLAs. For graceful degradation, we can define fallback model variants (lower precision or smaller model) and a soft-throttling policy that favors tail-latency-sensitive traffic.

I'm looping in Karthik to confirm ops constraints and Ben for cost/commit sizing. I'll also attach a one-page draft of "Headroom_Rules_v1.pdf" and a Draft_Autoscale_Pact for Procurement's review.

Want to schedule a 30-min alignment tomorrow? Proposed: 2029-05-10 09:00 PT.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: 2029-05-10T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial demand profile + burst ask for Dedicated pool -- ops proposal

Aisha / Ben — reviewed the forecast. High-level ops constraints and proposal below. I'm putting the operational pieces in plain language so Procurement has something deterministic for the SOW.

1) Baseline sizing
- Reserved pool: size to cover 1.25x baseline steady-state for safety. Baseline = average daily sustained tokens in the forecast (sheet: "Baseline").

2) Shoulder (soft headroom)
- Config: a shoulder slab sized to cover recurring weekly spikes up to 4x baseline for up to 3 hours. We model this as ephemeral GPUs drawn from an elastic slab; credits accrue monthly and can be used in scheduled windows.
- Eviction: shoulder slab is preemptible under fleet pressure. Preemption windows prioritized by: (1) non-latency-critical batch jobs, (2) shoulder slab for scheduled marketing windows, (3) shoulder for unscheduled bursts.

3) Autoscale pact rules (for SOW)
- Guaranteed baseline latency SLOs during baseline and shoulder-utilization <= 70%.
- For shoulder-utilization between 70-100%, Redwood will: (a) enable fallback model variant automatically, (b) apply soft-throttle (token shaping) with configured exceptions for high-priority routes.
- If shoulder eviction occurs due to fleet-wide constraints, Redwood will provide crediting (pro-rated) and a 4-hour escalation window with engineering on-call.

4) Runbook & telemetry
- We'll provide per-route token/latency dashboards, and an alerting policy tied to your marketing windows. The runbook will include postmortem obligations and a capacity-adjustment cadence.

Ben — can you add estimated committed GPU count and $/month delta for the proposed shoulder slab? Maya — if that looks reasonable, we'll fold these terms into the SOW for Procurement.

-Karthik
Director, Dedicated Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Maya Chen <maya@zentauri.ai>, Zentauri Procurement <procurement@zentauri.ai>
Date: 2029-05-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial demand profile + burst ask for Dedicated pool -- ops proposal

Quick cost sketch and commitment notes (summary for SOW):

- Estimated committed GPUs (baseline): 18 x A100-class (equivalent capacity) to cover 1.25x baseline across product lines.
- Shoulder slab: configurable 6-GPU ephemeral slab (preemptible) sized to cover 4x spikes for ~3 hours per week.
- Monthly delta (estimate): Reserved baseline band = $72,000/month; shoulder slab crediting = $6,500/month (includes pro-rated preemption insurance + monitoring).

Terms to include in SOW (suggested language):
1) Headroom allocation: Redwood will provide a shoulder slab sized as above. Shoulder is preemptible under defined conditions; Redwood will give 8 hours notice when preemption is scheduled for maintenance, and will provide post-event credits if unscheduled preemption causes measurable loss of traffic during scheduled marketing windows.
2) Autoscale pact: Redwood guarantees baseline latency SLOs for reserved pool. For shoulder-induced degradation, Redwood will execute the fallback model and soft-throttle policy and notify a Zentauri on-call contact.
3) Escalation & credits: If shoulder preemption occurs during a scheduled marketing window and causes >20% drop in successful requests vs forecast, Redwood will issue pro-rated service credits and initiate a joint postmortem within 48 hours.

Next steps: Aisha — push this into a single-page Ops Exhibit and share with Procurement. Maya/procurement — let us know if the crediting formula needs tweaks. Happy to hop on a quick call to finalize.

—Ben
VP, Infrastructure & Platform
Redwood Inference
